issues.failure_explanation: The proof explicitly needs the updated stacked matrix to be nonsingular, but the theorem neither assumes nor proves this for arbitrary admissible $\Phi$; $\tilde X_1$ is not even defined in the theorem statement. The omission is real: take the scalar $T$-palindromic polynomial $\lambda^2-\tfrac52\lambda+1$ with $X=[1,1]$, $\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(2,1/2)$, and $\Gamma=\tfrac23\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{bmatrix}$. Replace the eigenvalues by $3,1/3$, choose $\Phi=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $\tilde\Gamma_1=-\Gamma$. Then $\Phi\tilde\Gamma_1\Phi^T=\Gamma$, but $X\Phi=[1,0]$, so the updated stacked matrix has a zero second column and is singular. Correspondingly, the matrix whose inverse defines $\tilde A$ in (gg-10-1) is zero.
